item.title: nginx2root: pre-auth RCE in NGINX HTTP/2 (CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633) hits default configs; patches and public PoC out
item.description:
Breaking: On Wednesday, Nov 18, 2026 (~7 AM PT), F5/nginx shipped NGINX 1.31.9 and 1.30.7, which fix 10 CVEs. At the same time, Xint, Wiz, Rapid7, Metnir AI and Ikotas Labs disclosed "nginx2root". Several of these teams found the bugs independently. The two critical bugs are pre-auth remote code execution flaws in the HTTP/2 module (CVSS 9.2). CVE-2026-123007 is memory corruption (an integer underflow) in HTTP/2 flow control, present since 1.9.5 (2015). It hits the default config, even on servers that only serve static files. CVE-2026-123633 is an HTTP/2 use-after-free, mostly in reverse-proxy (proxy_pass) setups. Xint chained the nginx bugs with an unpatched Linux SCTP kernel zero-day to get from a container to host root. Researchers estimate millions of public servers are exposed (one estimate is 11.8M).

Exploitation status: Rapid7 has published a working RCE PoC for CVE-2026-123007. It needs ~128 GB of HTTP/2 traffic on one connection and lands as the nginx worker. That slows mass exploitation, but scanning is expected. As of ~9:45 AM PT, no in-the-wild exploitation is reported. Kubernetes ingress-nginx is reportedly still unpatched and has HTTP/2 on by default.

Do now: Upgrade to NGINX 1.31.9 / 1.30.7 (NGINX Plus 37.0.8.1 / 37.3.0.1). A full restart is required; a reload is not enough. Until you patch, set "http2 off;" on listeners. Block the sctp kernel module where you can.

Sources: nginx security advisories, Wiz Research, Xint (Brian Pak) on X, Wiz on X

item.title: Java4Shell: unauthenticated memory-corruption/RCE bug in OpenJDK 17+ (CVE-2026-114938) disclosed after leak, with Oracle patch out
item.description:
Breaking: Calif published technical details on Tuesday, Nov 17, 2026 (around 1 PM PT) for Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938, CVSS 4.0 score 9.2), an unauthenticated memory-corruption bug in OpenJDK HotSpot's AVX-512 VBMI Base64 decode intrinsic. The details had leaked earlier that morning. Any Java service that Base64-decodes attacker input (auth headers, tokens, uploads, messages) can hit it: a string of 'A' characters plus '=' triggers an out-of-bounds heap write. Calif shows Heartbleed-style memory disclosure and a path to remote code execution.

Affected: OpenJDK/Java SE 17.0.6 and later (Oracle lists 17, 21, 25 and 27 builds, plus GraalVM) on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI. Java 8 and 11 and ARM hosts are reportedly not affected. Oracle's Nov 17 Critical Patch Update fixes it. Temurin, Corretto and Zulu builds follow on their own schedules.

Exploitation status: Upwind says it reproduced exploitation privately. As of ~1:45 PM PT, no in-the-wild exploitation and no CISA KEV listing are reported. Unverified "exploits" on GitHub may be malware.

Do now: Patch Java runtimes, starting with internet-facing services and containers. Where you can't patch yet, set -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics (or -XX:UseAVX=2) and restart.

Sources: Calif write-up, Datadog Security Labs, Upwind, Calif on X

item.title: PHP2Shell update: CISA adds CVE-2026-109618/-109619 to KEV with an Oct 29 deadline after confirmed in-the-wild RCE
item.description:
Breaking update: CISA added both PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, unauthenticated RCE in PHP core) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Monday, Oct 26, 2026, with a remediation deadline of Thursday, Oct 29 and mandatory forensic triage under BOD 26-04.

The listing follows the first confirmed successful exploitation: honeypots running PHP 8.4.26 under Apache mod_php logged 35 shells from two IPs on Oct 24 using a chain matching the public proof of concept. Check Point reports attack traffic in the millions, with roughly 97.5% of visible PHP installs still unpatched as of Oct 23.

Patch to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35, restart Apache, PHP-FPM and workers, take unpatchable systems offline, and hunt for PHP workers spawning shells.

Sources: CISA alert, CISA KEV catalog, SecurityWeek, BleepingComputer

item.title: PHP2Shell: emergency PHP patches for two critical unauthenticated RCE flaws (CVE-2026-109618/-109619) as exploitation attempts begin
item.description:
Breaking: PHP released emergency fixes on Wednesday, Oct 21, 2026, around 7 AM PT for PHP2Shell, two critical (CVSS 9.2) flaws in the PHP runtime itself, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. They allow unauthenticated remote code execution and worker-memory reads on nearly every PHP version back to 5.4, across mod_php, PHP-FPM, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed, regardless of the application on top.

Cloudflare and watchTowr report in-the-wild exploitation attempts already underway (watchTowr says none successful yet), governments in the US, EU, UK and elsewhere issued urgent warnings, and organizations including Nintendo took sites offline. Kevin Beaumont called it one of the biggest vulns in years.

Patch now to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 (or your distro's backported package), then restart Apache, PHP-FPM and long-running workers. Isolate anything that can't be patched.

Sources: The Record, The Hacker News, Help Net Security, BleepingComputer

item.title: Citrix confirms actively exploited NetScaler RCE zero-days (CVE-2026-88771 / CVE-2026-88772)
item.description:
Breaking: Citrix confirmed two critical NetScaler ADC/Gateway remote code execution flaws were exploited as zero-days and released patches Sunday, Sep 27, 2026 (PT).

  • CVE-2026-88771 (CVSS 9.5): unauthenticated command execution via improper input validation. All NetScaler ADC and Gateway deployments are affected, including default configuration — no extra features required.
  • CVE-2026-88772 (CVSS 9.5): memory overflow leading to RCE or DoS when DTLS is enabled (DTLS is on by default for VPN virtual servers).

Vendor: "Exploits of CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 on unmitigated NetScaler deployments have been observed." Dutch NCSC and partners privately warned orgs over the weekend to take appliances offline ahead of disclosure. August builds that fixed CVE-2026-19490 remain vulnerable.

Patch now: 14.1-73.37 / 13.1-64.23 (and matching FIPS/NDcPP builds). Updating does not remove an already-present attacker — check Citrix IoCs / forensics.

Sources: Citrix CTX697096 · BleepingComputer
